Kitchen Fitting Labour Cost UK: A 2026 Guide

30 July 2026·BMB Renovation

If you are budgeting for a new kitchen, the cabinets and appliances are only part of the cost. Kitchen fitting labour can make up a substantial share of the overall spend, particularly where the room needs electrical, plumbing, flooring or structural work. As a rough UK guide, straightforward installation labour may fall somewhere around £2,000 to £5,000, while a more involved kitchen renovation can cost considerably more. These figures are only broad indications: every project differs, and the room size, layout, specification, access and location all affect the final price. Request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. This guide explains what kitchen fitting labour usually covers, which extras increase the price and how to compare quotations properly.

What is the typical kitchen fitting labour cost in the UK?

Kitchen fitting is usually priced either as a fixed project quotation, a day rate, or a combination of both. As a rough UK guide, a kitchen fitter’s labour rate may be around £200 to £350 per day, although rates vary by location, trade and the complexity of the work. Every project differs, so request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. Some installers price per cabinet, but this can make comparisons difficult because cabinet sizes, fillers, end panels and alterations are not always treated in the same way. For a standard kitchen with an uncomplicated layout, fitting-only labour is often priced as a complete package rather than as a simple number of days.

A basic installation could involve removing the old units, assembling and securing new cabinets, fitting doors and drawers, installing worktops, and making the final connections for appliances. A modest room with limited changes may take several working days. A larger kitchen, an island, bespoke storage, solid-surface worktops or a changed layout can take longer and require several trades. When requesting a quote, ask whether the price includes VAT and whether waste removal, delivery handling and finishing work are included.

What is normally included in a fitting quote?

  • Protection of suitable floors, nearby surfaces and access routes, where required.
  • Removal of existing kitchen units, subject to the agreed scope of work.
  • Assembly, levelling and fixing of base units, wall units, tall units and panels.
  • Fitting doors, drawers, handles, plinths, cornices, pelmets and fillers.
  • Installation and cutting of standard laminate worktops, if specified in the quotation.
  • Fitting sinks, taps and appliances, with connections completed by the appropriate trades.
  • Basic making-good, adjustment of doors and drawers, and a final check of the installation.

Which extra tasks increase kitchen fitting labour costs?

The biggest difference between a simple fitting job and a full renovation is the amount of preparation and alteration needed before the cabinets can be installed. Moving a sink, dishwasher, cooker or washing machine may require new plumbing and waste runs. Changing the position of an oven or adding appliances can mean new electrical circuits, additional sockets or changes to the consumer unit. Electrical work should be clearly identified in the quote and completed by an appropriately qualified professional.

  • Removing and disposing of old units, flooring, wall coverings or bulky appliances.
  • Moving water, waste, gas or electrical services to suit a new layout.
  • Installing extra sockets, lighting, extractor systems or appliance supplies.
  • Repairing uneven walls, damaged plaster, floors or subfloors before fitting.
  • Fitting tiles, splashbacks, new flooring, skirting boards or decorative finishes.
  • Cutting and installing quartz, granite, porcelain or other specialist worktops.
  • Building or removing partitions, widening openings, or carrying out structural alterations.
  • Working in a difficult-to-access property where parking, stairs or restricted delivery space add time.

Labour-only kitchen fitting versus a full renovation

A labour-only quote assumes that you have bought the cabinets, panels, worktops, appliances and other materials. This can reduce the headline price, but you remain responsible for checking quantities, compatibility, delivery, missing parts and damaged items. If a required component is unavailable, the fitter may need to return on another day, potentially adding labour.

A full kitchen renovation quote may coordinate several parts of the project, including plumbing, electrical work, cabinet installation, tiling, flooring and decorating. That can make the total easier to understand because the work is planned as one sequence. How to compare kitchen fitting quotes fairly

The cheapest quotation is not necessarily the lowest-cost option if important tasks have been excluded. Give each contractor the same kitchen plan, product list and specification, then ask for an itemised quotation. It should separate labour, materials, specialist work and provisional sums wherever possible. Check whether the quote covers removal, waste, delivery, worktop templating, appliance connections, plumbing, electrics, tiling, flooring, decorating and final cleaning.

  • Confirm the exact work included and identify anything described only as ‘to be confirmed’.
  • Check whether VAT is included and whether the price is fixed or based on an estimated number of days.
  • Ask who supplies fixings, sealant, trim, adhesives, pipework and other small materials.
  • Confirm responsibility for measuring and checking the kitchen before ordering.
  • Ask how variations are approved if hidden damage or design changes are discovered.
  • Check the expected start date, approximate duration and payment stages.
  • Make sure specialist work, appliance connections and any relevant certification requirements are addressed.
  • Compare the same specification rather than comparing totals from different scopes of work.

Ways to keep kitchen fitting labour under control

Keeping the existing layout is often one of the simplest ways to reduce labour because it may avoid moving plumbing, waste and electrical supplies. Ordering all cabinets and components in good time can also prevent delays, but do not arrange delivery until measurements and the final design have been checked. Keep a clear product schedule showing cabinet codes, panels, handles, appliances and worktop details. If the kitchen is being supplied by a separate retailer, ask the fitter to review the plan before you place the order.

It is also worth deciding early whether you want a basic refresh or a complete renovation. Replacing doors and worktops may need less labour than removing every unit and changing the layout, although the condition of the existing cabinets matters. Conversely, cutting corners on preparation can lead to poor alignment, leaks, damaged surfaces or extra remedial work. A detailed survey and written scope are usually more useful than relying on a single headline fitting price. Frequently Asked Questions

How much does kitchen fitting labour cost in the UK?+
As a rough guide, straightforward kitchen fitting labour may cost around £2,000 to £5,000, but complex layouts, additional trades and specialist materials can raise the price. Every project is different, so request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
What does a kitchen fitter’s day rate include?+
A day rate normally covers the fitter’s labour for agreed installation work. It may not include materials, waste disposal, plumbing, electrical work, tiling, decorating or specialist worktop installation, so check the quotation.
Is kitchen fitting labour cheaper if I buy the kitchen myself?+
It can be, but only if the design, quantities and components are correct. You may also need to arrange delivery, deal with missing parts and pay for return visits if the kitchen is not ready to install.
How long does it take to fit a kitchen?+
A straightforward kitchen may take several working days. A full renovation involving rewiring, plumbing changes, flooring, tiling or structural alterations can take substantially longer.
Should a kitchen fitting quote include plumbing and electrical work?+
It should clearly state whether those tasks are included, excluded or priced separately. Ask for them to be listed individually so you can compare quotations on the same basis.
